title: India-origin cricketer Reddy handed 8-year ban by ICC for corruption
content: USA cricketer Bodugum Akhilesh Reddy has been banned from all cricket for eight years after an ICC tribunal found him guilty of three Anti-Corruption Code breaches linked to the 2025 Abu Dhabi T10. He was found to have attempted match-fixing, encouraged a teammate to participate, and deleted evidence during the investigation. His ban is effective from November 21, 2025.

title: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna says quantum computing is closer than many think
content: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna believes quantum computing will impact business within years.  He stated quantum advantage research shows efficiency over classical machines.  Krishna explained recent stock declines stemmed from delayed customer deals.  Companies are reassessing spending priorities due to advanced AI models.  IBM sees no disruption to its software business from AI.

title: Government proposes sweeping tax rule changes to attract offshore funds - what it means
content: The Bill, which has been circulated among Members of Parliament, is expected to be introduced in the Lok Sabha shortly by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

title: India to build over 1,000 affordable homes in Seychelles
content: India will construct over one thousand affordable housing units in Seychelles. This project addresses the island nation's housing shortage and strengthens bilateral cooperation. The first phase of this development is scheduled for completion by the year 2029. India's National Buildings Construction Corporation will manage the entire project's planning and implementation. This initiative is part of a larger economic package and development partnership between the two nations.

title: Mark Zuckerberg lays off 8,000 employees, spends $130B on AI
content: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg says AI has “net created a lot of jobs” thanks to the massive infrastructure buildout, dismissing fears of AI job losses. His remarks come months after Meta laid off 8,000 employees—10% of its workforce—in an AI-first restructuring, while committing $130-145 billion to AI spending in 2026. Meta’s Q2 free cash flow crashed 91% as shares fell 10%, even as revenue jumped 28% to $60.8 billion.

title: Cambridge student, 12, turns movement into energy, eyes $25K prize
content: A 12-year-old Cambridge student, Ahmed Abdelsalam, has created VERDA, a system that captures energy from movement like walking, wind and waves. His clean energy idea has earned him a place among 10 finalists in the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge, where he will compete for a $25,000 prize.

title: Meet the king snake that hunts and eats venomous snakes
content: Kingsnakes are non-venomous constrictors famous for hunting venomous snakes.  These adaptable hunters also consume lizards, rodents, birds, and amphibians.  Kingsnakes possess a natural resistance to pit viper venom, aiding their survival.  They inhabit diverse North American environments from coast to coast.  These reptiles play a vital role in controlling rodent and snake populations.

title: Jeff Bezos warns Mamdani on NYC taxes, slams wasteful spending
content: Jeff Bezos commented on New York City's proposed pied-à-terre tax, calling it a fine thing for the city. He cautioned against aggressive tax increases, which could deter tourism and economic competitiveness. Bezos rejected targeting individuals like Ken Griffin, calling it a villain strategy. He argued that government spending inefficiencies are a greater concern than taxation levels. Bezos previously criticized New York City's public school spending and economic policies.

title: Nanaji Deshmukh Awas Yojana: How workers can avail Rs 1.6 lakh housing aid
content: In Gujarat, registered construction workers have the opportunity to benefit from financial support aimed at housing through the Shree Nanaji Deshmukh Awas Yojana. To qualify, applicants must have been registered with the welfare board for a minimum of two years. Following the acquisition of an e-Nirman Card and house allotment, they can submit their applications. Those approved will receive ₹1.6 lakh to assist in home ownership.

title: Michael Phelps' $100M fortune in 2026: Endorsements, investments and luxury life
content: Michael Phelps turned his legendary Olympic achievements into a multi-million dollar empire. By securing high-value endorsements from renowned brands post-retirement, he also channeled his success into impactful ventures. His establishment of a foundation showcases his commitment to youth education in swimming and healthy living. Additionally, Phelps's investment in the mental health platform shows his suppport for emotional wellness.

title: BJP holds Manjalpur in Gujarat, but with a much smaller victory margin
content: In a recent bypoll, the BJP claimed victory in the Manjalpur seat of Vadodara, Gujarat, with candidate Satish Patel triumphing over Congress's Bhikhabhai Rabari by a notable, though diminished, margin compared to past assembly election results. This election followed the passing of BJP MLA Yogesh Patel, highlighting a need for the party to reassess its strategies given the reduced lead in votes.

title: After Arjuna Awardee calls out Indian calendar, AICF moves to find solution
content: The All India Chess Federation (AICF) is working to hold the senior National Chess Championship in November-December 2026 after it was initially scheduled for March 2027. Following concerns raised by Grandmaster Abhijeet Gupta, the federation is in talks with stakeholders to finalise dates. AICF said a packed domestic and international calendar had forced the initial postponement.

title: TN SSLC supplementary result 2026 out: Check Class 10 marks here
content: Tamil Nadu Directorate of Government Examinations has announced the SSLC Class 10 supplementary results. Students can check their marks memo on the official website tnresults.nic.in. They will need their exam roll number and date of birth to access results. This announcement allows successful candidates to proceed with Class 11 admissions. Original marksheets will be available from respective schools later.

title: Glide bombs: How these cheap weapons are giving Russia its battlefield edge back in Ukraine
content: The Ukraine conflict showcases new combat innovations, especially Russian glide bombs. These weapons allow strikes from safe distances, protecting aircraft from enemy defenses. Russia uses conversion kits and purpose-built munitions to leverage vast bomb stockpiles effectively. India is also developing its own glide bombs for deep strike capabilities. These advancements aim to hit targets with reduced risk to aircrew.

title: 'Abusing is not cool': Manu Bhaker's social media post goes viral
content: Manu Bhaker, who won two medals at the Paris Olympics, shared a long message on X on Sunday. She did not mention any particular incident but spoke about the increasing use of abusive language in everyday conversations. Manu created history at the Paris Olympics 2024 by becoming the first Indian athlete in the post-Independence era to win two medals at a single Olympic Games.

title: Eyes in the sky: How India plans to detect & destroy every airborne threat before it strikes
content: India is significantly expanding its airborne surveillance fleet to bolster air defence capabilities.  New Netra Mk-1A aircraft will triple the indigenous fleet size by 2028.  The Netra Mk-2 program aims for advanced indigenous AWACS platforms by 2032.  This expansion will increase the fleet from six to eighteen aircraft.  These systems will provide comprehensive battlespace awareness and networked force capabilities.

title: Rakul Preet Singh reveals what drew her to play Shurpanakha in 'Ramayana'
content: Rakul Preet Singh, who plays Shurpanakha in Nitesh Tiwari and Namit Malhotra's magnum opus, 'Ramayana Part 1', responded to a fan's heartfelt letter on X (previously Twitter), revealing that the character's complexity was exactly what drew her to the role. The actress said she hopes audiences approach Shurpanakha's story with an open mind when the film releases, amid continued buzz around the 'Ramayana: The Introduction' trailer which dropped last week at Brahma Mahurat on July 30, 2026.

title: California woman rescued after being swept down Kern River rapids
content: A woman was pulled to safety after falling into California's Kern River. First responders found her partially submerged beneath a rock outcropping near a steep cliff. They used a life jacket and rescue rope to bring her out of the water. The Kern County Sheriff's Office shared dramatic video footage of the successful rescue. Officials warned the public about the river's extreme dangers and the need for caution.

title: Infantino: The man who tried to sell football
content: How FIFA’s self-styled ‘King of Soccer’ tried to smuggle private equity through football’s gates, only for the game’s warring tribes to unite and burn the horse.

title: Faridabad school teacher stabbed to death by masked man; CCTV captures attack
content: In a tragic incident at a local school, a 26-year-old teacher was brutally stabbed by a masked assailant. Reports indicate that the attacker waited near the classroom before launching a sudden assault with a knife. Surveillance footage documented the horrifying event, leading to the victim's death. Authorities are actively investigating this shocking crime and are on the hunt for the unidentified attacker.

title: 'No excuses if you want to play for India': The philosophy that shaped Auqib Nabi
content: On Monday, Jammu and Kashmir seamer Auqib Nabi replaced injured Jasprit Bumrah in the India squad for the upcoming two-match Test tour of Sri Lanka. With his maiden call-up to the senior national team, he became the first player from the valley to get selected in India's Test squad. The J&K seamer's rise is driven by a simple philosophy: if you want to play for India, excuses are not an option.

title: Buffalo Sabres linked to former $13.5M Dallas Stars winger in free agency
content: Michael Bunting struggled in the last season as his contract expired and he has turned into an unrestricted free agent. Ahead of training camp, the Buffalo Sabres have been linked to him.

title: Unhappy over non-inclusion in Karnataka Cabinet, 2 Congress MLAs resign
content: Two Congress MLAs resigned from the Karnataka Legislative Assembly on Monday.  They were unhappy over their exclusion from the state cabinet expansion.  Supporters of one MLA protested, alleging unfair treatment by the party.  Twenty ministers are set to take their oath later today.  These resignations intensify discontent within the ruling party.

title: California’s hottest luxury homes are getting cheaper. But why?
content: The luxury real estate market in Palm Springs is witnessing notable price drops following an unprecedented surge. Properties are lingering on the market longer and frequently selling for less than their listed prices. This trend suggests a cooling off as inventory levels rise. On average, home values have slightly dipped compared to last year, marking a shift after a period driven by remote work opportunities and attractive low rates.

title: Bank holidays in August 2026: Where and when banks will remain closed this month
content: August brings numerous bank holidays across India, affecting branch operations.  Banks will close on specific dates due to regional festivals and national observances.  Customers should verify local branch availability before planning visits.  Digital banking services will remain accessible throughout these holiday periods.  Plan branch-specific transactions in advance to avoid any inconvenience.

title: Who was Natasha Ward? Australian middle-distance runner dies at 21
content: Australian middle-distance runner Natasha Ward has died at 21, NSW Athletics and the Sutherland District Athletics Club confirmed in a joint statement on Thursday, July 30. Ward competed across the 400m, 800m and 1500m, racing at the 2024 Australian Championships against Morgan Mitchell and Claudia Hollingsworth, and had recently won bronze at the UniSport Nationals while studying at Macquarie University.

title: Students outnumbered by 'puncture banane wale' at Jantar Mantar protest: BJP neta
content: BJP leader Ramesh Bidhuri alleged locksmiths and puncture repairers outnumbered students at a recent protest. He criticized the abusive language used against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his family. Bidhuri claimed opposition leaders misled youth into gathering at Jantar Mantar for the protest. Prime Minister Modi expressed pain over abuses directed at his late mother. He called for forgiving the misguided youth and guiding them instead.

title: The rain keeps falling, the death toll keeps rising
content: Southwest monsoon has caused widespread devastation across Assam, Gujarat, and Kerala. Assam reported the highest death toll, with 82 people dead and nearly 1.78 lakh affected. Gujarat faced severe flooding after heavy rainfall, recording 35 rain-related deaths. Kerala battled rain-induced landslides and flash floods, leaving 15 people dead. Relief operations are ongoing in all affected states.

title: Jana Nayagan box office day 12: Vijay’s film slows after Rs 200 crore mark

However, the film has recently seen a decrease in daily earnings as it began its second week. Current estimates reveal that the total collections in India have reached Rs 206.38 crore, marking a slight slowdown in momentum.

title: What time will stock market close from today? New timings and rationale explained
content: The Closing Auction Session aims to concentrate liquidity at the end of the trading day. The idea is to facilitate smoother execution of large orders and generate a closing price that is more accurate in terms of reflecting overall market demand and supply.

title: Russia floats out nuclear submarine: What makes Project 885M Yasen-M special
content: The Sevmash shipyard has unveiled Russia's latest Yasen-M nuclear submarine, named Ulyanovsk. This cutting-edge vessel will undergo rigorous testing before it officially joins the Northern Fleet. The Yasen-M class marks a major advancement in Russia's naval power, integrating capabilities for both anti-submarine and land-attack operations alongside state-of-the-art armament. The Russian Navy anticipates welcoming this sophisticated submarine by December 2027.

title: Lok Sabha clears bill to increase number of Supreme Court judges, without debate

The legislation will now be sent to the Rajya Sabha for its consideration. The government argues this increase will improve judicial efficiency and speed. The sanctioned strength was last increased in 2019.
